paper_sections.title: Altered regional activity and connectivity of functional brain networks in congenital unilateral conductive hearing loss
3.2 Differences in regional activity and connectivity
Ethics approval and consent to participate

description.value: The study investigated regional spontaneous brain activity, local synchrony, and seed-based functional connectivity in patients with right-sided congenital unilateral microtia and severe hearing loss compared with age- and sex-matched normal-hearing controls, and examined associations with hearing and clinical variables.

design.value: This retrospective case-control study compared 24 patients with right-sided congenital unilateral microtia and 25 age- and sex-matched normal-hearing individuals using resting-state fMRI. ALFF, fALFF, ReHo, and seed-based functional connectivity were analyzed with and without global signal regression, and clinical correlations were assessed.

description.value: Hearing level was assessed by pure tone audiometry in a closed field at six frequencies (0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4 and 8 kHz).
Cognitive abilities were evaluated using the Mini-Mental State Examination.
Cognitive abilities were evaluated using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment test.
27 patients aged 11–40 years with right-sided congenital unilateral microtia; finally, 24 patients with UM were included.

description.value: Functional images were obtained axially with a gradient echo type echo planar imaging (EPI) sequence. The scanning parameters were 36 slices, thickness of 4 mm, gap of 0 mm, 64 × 64 acquisition matrix, flip-angle of 90°, and field of view of 200 × 200 mm².

pulse_sequence_type.value: gradient echo type echo planar imaging (EPI) sequence

instrument.value: GE750 3.0 T MR scanner with an eight-channel standard quadrature head coil

description.value: Anatomical images were acquired with a high-resolution T1-weighted gradient-echo sequence. Parameters included a thickness of 1 mm, 192 slices, and a field of view of 256 × 256 mm².

All rs-fMRI images were processed using SPM12 and SeeCAT. The first 10 time points were deleted. Slice-timing and head-motion correction were implemented; corrected images were normalized to the EPI template, resampled to 3-mm isotropic voxels, smoothed with a 4-mm full-width at half maximum Gaussian kernel, regressed for confounding signals, temporally band-pass filtered at 0.01–0.1 Hz, and scrubbed for motion-related effects.

steps.value: The first 10 time points of the functional imaging were deleted.
Slice-timing and head-motion correction were implemented.
The corrected images were normalized to the EPI template.
Images were resampled to 3-mm isotropic voxels.
Images were smoothed with a 4-mm full-width at half maximum Gaussian kernel.
Signals from white matter and cerebrospinal fluid, linear drift, and Friston-24 head-motion parameters were removed using a linear regression model.
The time series for each voxel was temporally band-pass filtered at 0.01–0.1 Hz.
Any volume with a >0.5 mm framewise displacement, as well as its adjacent volumes (two forward and one backward frames), was replaced using linear interpolated data.

description.value: rs-fMRI data were analyzed with global signal regression during preprocessing.

steps.value: Global signal regression uses linear regression to remove the global signal from the time series of each voxel.

description.value: rs-fMRI data were analyzed without global signal regression during preprocessing.

steps.value: Global signal regression was not used.

model_settings.value: ALFF, fALFF, ReHo and SBFC were compared in the two groups with regression of age, gender and educational level. Gaussian random field corrections used p < 0.001 at the voxel level and p < 0.05 at the cluster level.

The average time series of the BOLD signal was extracted from the seed. Temporal correlations between this reference time series and the time courses of all other brain voxels were calculated, and correlation coefficients were transformed to z values using Fisher's r-to-z transformation.

model_type.value: two-sample t-test and Fisher's exact test

model_settings.value: Categorical data in the two groups were compared using Fisher’s exact test, whereas continuous data were compared using two-sample t-tests.

estimator.value: Fisher's exact test and two-sample t-tests

model_settings.value: ROI-wise Pearson’s correlation analysis was used to investigate the relationship between brain regions showing group differences and clinical features. Statistical significance was defined as p < 0.05 with the Bonferroni correction.

description.value: Subjects lay still and relaxed with their eyes closed, were instructed not to fall asleep, and were instructed not to think of anything.

definition.value: Compared with controls, patients with UM had higher ALFF values in the left inferior temporal gyrus and precuneus.

interpretations.value: ALFF was considered an effective indicator of the spontaneous neural activity of specific regions.

definition.value: Compared with controls, patients with UM had lower ALFF values in the left temporal pole, superior temporal gyrus, middle temporal gyrus, and medial prefrontal cortex.

definition.value: Compared with controls, the UM group had higher fALFF values in the left inferior temporal gyrus and fusiform.

interpretations.value: fALFF was found to be more stable in detecting regional spontaneous neural activity during the resting state by suppressing physiological noise.

definition.value: Compared with controls, the UM group had higher ReHo values in the left inferior temporal gyrus.

interpretations.value: Increased ReHo indicates a stronger local synchronization of signals with neighboring voxels.

definition.value: Compared with controls, subjects in the UM group showed higher connectivity from the left inferior temporal gyrus seed with the left inferior parietal gyrus and inferior frontal gyrus.

interpretations.value: Seed-based functional connectivity analysis was performed to determine the functional coordination between a given grey matter voxel and other voxels within the brain.
